answers.question: List of scenarios
answers.answer: Three scenarios were used: 1) Orderly (NGFS Net-Zero 2050) – likely warming 1.4°C (ranging from 1.0 to 1.8°C) [SSP1 - RCP 1.9]; 2) Disorderly (NGFS Delayed Transition) – likely warming 2.7°C (ranging from 2.1 to 3.5°C) [SSP2 - RCP 4.5]; 3) Hot House World (NGFS Current Policies) – likely warming 3.6°C (ranging from 2.8 to 4.6°C) [SSP3 - RCP 7.0].

answers.question: Co-produced climate scenarios
answers.answer: HNZ did not co-produce its climate scenarios with external stakeholders in the traditional sense. In FY24, Hollard commissioned an external climate advisory team to facilitate more than 10 climate workshops with the Climate-related Disclosure Working Group (CRDWG) to test exposure and vulnerability to climate-related physical and transition risks by adopting three climate scenarios from internationally recognised sources (IPCC and NGFS). In FY25, Hollard reassessed and reaffirmed those scenarios without new co-production. The scenarios used are: Orderly (SSP1-RCP1.9, ~1.4°C), Disorderly (SSP2-RCP4.5, ~2.7°C), and Hot House World (SSP3-RCP7.0, ~3.6°C).
answers.evidence: In FY24 Hollard commissioned an external climate advisory team to facilitate more than 10 climate workshops with the Climate-related Disclosure Working Group (CRDWG) to test our exposure and vulnerability to climate-related physical and transition risks by adopting three climate scenarios (see top row headings in Table 2. scenario analysis) from internationally recognised sources, such as the IPCC and the Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS).
answers.notes: The scenarios were developed in FY24 via external advisory-facilitated workshops and reaffirmed in FY25. They are based on IPCC/NGFS frameworks, not co-produced with communities or regulators, but with an external climate advisory team and internal working group.

answers.question: Damage from acute physical risk considered
answers.answer: Yes. HNZ considers acute physical risks including extreme rain and flood, bushfires, storms, and cyclones. Customers are exposed through damage to and loss of insured assets such as motor vehicles and homes. Claim expenses from catastrophe events are used as a proxy for the financial impacts of climate physical risk. Capital modelling includes quarterly stress testing to assess the impact of catastrophe risk (a type of acute physical climate risk) on capital.
answers.evidence: Acute physical risks: extreme rain and flood, bushfires, storms, and cyclones... Our customers are exposed to physical climate risks through damage to, and loss of, insured assets such as motor vehicles and homes. The increasing frequency and severity of weather events over time may outstrip Hollard's ability to provide affordable insurance products or deliver the expected levels of customer service... Capital modelling and management: Hollard conducts quarterly stress testing to assess the impact of catastrophe risk (a type of acute physical climate risk) on capital, in line with the ICAAP. The stress scenarios considered include a single extreme event as well as multiple large events... Claims from catastrophe events are considered a proxy for the financial impacts of climate physical-risk.

answers.answer:
HNZ used three climate scenarios at a global scale, based on NGFS and IPCC frameworks:

3. Hot House World – likely warming 3.6°C (ranging from 2.8 to 4.6°C) [SSP3 - RCP 7.0], aligned to NGFS Current Policies

answers.question: Time frames
answers.answer: HNZ uses three time horizons for climate scenario analysis: Short-term (Present day – 2030), Medium-term (2030–2040), and Long-term (2040–2050). For risk management, Hollard focuses on a shorter time horizon (less than 1 year) for material risks and a longer-term horizon (more than 1 year) for emerging material risks. The time horizons for scenario analysis are defined as 20-year averages around the nominated year (e.g., 2030 is the average of 2020 to 2039; 2050 is the average of 2040 to 2059).
answers.evidence: "HNZ continued to select 2030, 2040 and 2050 as the time horizons for climate scenario analysis, based on the tenure of HNZ's existing partnerships, its strategic planning timeframe and assessing meaningful timeframes where there has been material development in the climate scenarios to compare across the scenarios." ... "Hollard's risk management approach focuses on the shorter time horizon (less than 1 year) in managing its material risks and will consider a longer-term horizon (more than 1 year) in managing its emerging material risks (including the compounding effect of physical and transition risk) in the long term."

answers.question: Justification for scenario/model choice
answers.answer: HNZ justified its scenario/model choices based on three considerations: (1) Industry specificity — aligning climate scenario analysis to industry bodies for peer comparability, leading to adoption of NGFS scenarios (Orderly/Net-Zero 2050, Disorderly/Delayed Transition, Hot House World/Current Policies); (2) NZ CS 1 requirements — which mandate a minimum of three warming scenarios including a 1.5°C scenario, a 3°C or greater scenario, and a third scenario; and (3) Inclusion of a balanced spread of scenarios — covering low warming (SSP1-RCP 1.9), medium warming (SSP2-RCP 4.5), and high warming (SSP3-RCP 7.0).
answers.evidence: "When determining the global warming scenarios, HNZ considered: • Industry specificity: ensuring our climate scenario analysis is aligned to industry bodies and to be easily compared with peers. This led to the adoption of the Orderly (NGFS Net-Zero 2050), Disorderly (NGFS Delayed Transition) and Hot House World (NGFS Current Policies) scenarios. • The requirements of NZ CS 1: NZ CS 1 requires the adoption of a minimum of three warming scenarios, including a 1.5 degrees Celsius climate-related scenario, a three degrees Celsius or greater climate-related scenario, and a third climate-related scenario. • Inclusion of a balanced spread of the scenarios: low warming ([SSP1- RCP 1.9]), medium warming ( [SSP2 – RCP 4.5]), and high warming ([SSP3 – RCP 7.0]) scenarios."
answers.location_hint: Page 6 of the HNZ CRD Climate Statement
answers.notes: The justification is explicitly and comprehensively stated in the document. The scenarios were originally developed in FY24 with the help of an external climate advisory team and reaffirmed in FY25.

answers.question: Direct and indirect physical climate risks
answers.answer: HNZ is exposed to both acute and chronic physical climate risks, primarily indirectly through the assets it insures. Acute physical risks include extreme rain and flood, bushfires, storms, and cyclones. Chronic physical risks include rising sea-level and increases in temperature. HNZ does not own any property, plant and equipment or right-of-use leased assets, so no physical assets are directly exposed to climate-related physical risks. Customers are exposed through damage to and loss of insured assets such as motor vehicles and homes.

Our customers are exposed to physical climate risks through damage to, and loss of, insured assets such as motor vehicles and homes. ... HNZ does not own any property, plant and equipment or right-of-use leased assets, therefore no physical assets are directly exposed to climate-related physical risks."
